lines.japanese: 夜勤明けの俺を起こしたのは、空気を読まない携帯電話の着信音だった。
lines.english: What woke me after my night shift was the tactless ring of my cell phone.

lines.japanese: 発信者を確認するのさえ億劫で、俺はケータイを掴むとダイレクトに耳へ当てた。
lines.english: Even checking who it was felt like too much trouble. I grabbed the phone and put it straight to my ear.
“Nn... Who is this...?”

lines.japanese: 『おうドラ。俺、俺。成田工務店のエグゼクティブ・マネージャー』
lines.english: “Yo, Dora. It's me. Executive manager of Narita Construction.”

lines.japanese: そんな役職に覚えはないが、そんな馬鹿を言いだす馬鹿な声には覚えがあった。
lines.english: I didn't remember any such position, but I did recognize the idiot voice making that idiotic claim.

lines.japanese: 「エージかよ……」
lines.english: “Eiji...”

lines.japanese: 俺はベッドの上、悶えるように寝返りを打った。
lines.english: I rolled over on the bed with a groan.

lines.japanese: 眠りに着くまで一緒だった女はもういない。やつの寝巻は枕元に畳まれ、代わりに壁にかかっていた制服が消えている。
lines.english: The woman who'd been with me when I fell asleep was already gone. Her pajamas were folded beside my pillow, and the uniform that had hung on the wall was gone in their place.

lines.japanese: 『馬鹿おまえ、喜べって！　吉報だよ、吉報。金ない職ないロクでもないでお馴染みのおまえに、仏のようなエージ様から超ビッグニュース！　イェイ、イェーッ！』
lines.english: “Come on, man, be happy! I've got great news. Huge news from the Buddha-like Lord Eiji for the famously broke, jobless loser himself! Yeah! Yeeeah!”

lines.japanese: 寝起きにはイラッと来るテンションだった。
lines.english: His energy was infuriating first thing after waking up.

lines.japanese: 『実はな、すんげえ楽で儲かる仕事があんだよ。成田工務店に依頼してやるから。いやいや、そんな礼なんていいから。でェ、内容なんだけどォ』
lines.english: “See, I've got this crazy easy job that pays great. I'll place the order with Narita Construction. No, no, no need to thank me. Now, here's the gig—”

lines.japanese: 「聞かねえよ。だぁら、成田工務店はもう廃業しましたつっただろ。長年のご愛顧ありがとうございましたコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Not listening. I told you, Narita Construction is out of business. Thanks for all your years of patronage, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 『あ、そーだっけ？　まあ、それはいいや』
lines.english: “Oh, right. Was it? Well, never mind that.”

lines.japanese: 「よくねーよ」
lines.english: “I mind.”

lines.japanese: 『いや、仕事っつーかさ、ちょっと預かり物してもらうだけなの。単純に友達として頼むよ』
lines.english: “It's barely even a job. I just need you to hold on to something for me. I'm asking you as a friend.”

lines.japanese: 「友達じゃねーし」
lines.english: “We're not friends.”

lines.japanese: 『なァーんで！　冷たいことゆぅ～なよォ～、ドラぁ～』
lines.english: “Whyyyy? Don't be so coooold, Doraaa.”

lines.japanese: 「甘えンな。かわいくねえ」
lines.english: “Don't whine. It isn't cute.”

lines.japanese: 「だいたいおまえ、俺が便利屋やってたころだって、ロクな仕事持って来なかったじゃねーか。毎度毎度あぶない橋渡らせてくれたよなァ、おお」
lines.english: “Even back when I was a handyman, you never brought me a decent job. Every damn time, you made me walk a tightrope.”

lines.japanese: 『ハア？　なんだよ、マンション麻雀の代打ちさせたことまだ根に持ってんの？　言ったじゃん、ありゃ合法なんだって。あの場では現金の譲渡なんて一切なかったろ？』
lines.english: “Huh? You're still mad about the time I had you sit in at that apartment mahjong game? I told you, it was legal. Nobody exchanged a single yen in cash there, did they?”

lines.japanese: 「ふざけんなてめえ。医者と実業家と元プロ野球選手がコソコソ集まって、図書券の奪い合いで済むわけねーだろ。本いっぱい読みたかったら本屋ごとまるまる一件買える連中じゃねーか」
lines.english: “Screw you. A doctor, a businessman, and an ex-pro baseball player don't sneak into an apartment to fight over bookstore vouchers. If those guys wanted books that badly, they could buy the whole damn store.”

lines.japanese: 『えっ？　うそ、おまえもしかして、賭博行為を疑ってたの？　うわ、マジかよ、俺そんなこと思いもしなかったわ』
lines.english: “What? No way. You thought there was gambling going on? Wow, seriously? The idea never even crossed my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「白々しい……」
lines.english: “You're so full of shit...”

lines.japanese: 『ま、済んだことをクヨクヨしてても仕方ねーって。元気出せよ、次から気を付けりゃいいんだ』
lines.english: “No point brooding over the past. Cheer up. You learned your lesson, so just be more careful next time.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、その通りだ。ってわけで交渉決裂だ、切るぞ」
lines.english: “You're right. Which means negotiations are over. I'm hanging up.”

lines.japanese: 『アアーちょっと待て１万出す１万！』
lines.english: “Aah, wait! Ten grand! I'll give you ten grand!”

lines.japanese: 「額の問題じゃねンだよ、ヤベえことしたくねえつってんの」
lines.english: “The amount isn't the problem. I said I'm done doing dangerous shit.”

lines.japanese: １万──正直、魅力的なギャランティではあった。
lines.english: Ten thousand yen. Honestly, it was a tempting fee.

lines.japanese: しかしいまの俺は、かつての消えゆくさだめから解放された、ひとりの全き人間だ。
lines.english: But I was a whole human being now, freed from the fate that once had me vanishing away.

lines.japanese: いまでは守りたいものもある。勝ちとりたい未来もある。便利屋をたたみ、通院もはじめて、これからは堅実に生きると決めた。
lines.english: Now I had things I wanted to protect and a future I wanted to win. I'd closed the handyman business, started going to the hospital, and decided to live a steady life from here on out.

lines.japanese: いくら積まれても譲れないもの、それは言いかえれば男の誇りだ。
lines.english: What no amount of money could make me surrender was, in other words, my pride as a man.

lines.japanese: 『分かった、５万！』
lines.english: “Fine. Fifty grand!”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 男の誇りが揺らぐ額だった。
lines.english: That was enough to shake a man's pride.

lines.japanese: 『いや、一ヵ月ぐらい鍵を一個預かってほしいんだ。そんだけ、マジそんだけ！』
lines.english: “I only need you to hold on to one key for about a month. That's it. Seriously, that's all!”

lines.japanese: 「……え、そんだけなの」
lines.english: “...Wait, that's all?”

lines.japanese: 『ま、基本的には。そんで、そんだけで５万。どーよ』
lines.english: “Basically. And fifty grand just for that. What do you say?”

lines.japanese: どうもこうもない。めちゃめちゃ美味い話だ。
lines.english: What was there to say? It was an insanely sweet deal.

lines.japanese: しかし美味い話には裏があるってのが、世の常、ひとの常、エージの常。
lines.english: But sweet deals always came with a catch. That was the way of the world, the way of people, and the way of Eiji.

lines.japanese: しかし５万。それだけあれば何ができる。
lines.english: Still, fifty thousand yen. What could I do with that much?

lines.japanese: 念願のジム通いはできるか。インターネットってやつは買えるのか。最近バイクにもちょっと興味出てきたけど、免許を取るにはどのくらいの金がかかるんだろう。
lines.english: Could I finally join a gym? Could I buy this Internet thing? I'd gotten a little interested in motorcycles lately too. How much did a license cost?

lines.japanese: いや、それより旅行だ。鳴を旅行に連れていける。俺の前じゃ口にしないけど、やつはプラチナが故郷の温泉街について語るたび、並々ならぬ関心を寄せるらしい。
lines.english: No, better yet, a trip. I could take Naru somewhere. She never mentioned it around me, but apparently whenever Platinum talked about the hot-spring town she called home, Naru showed an extraordinary interest.

lines.japanese: 「あの、ちょっと参考までに聞くけど。え、何なの、その鍵って。ソレにはどんな裏があんの」
lines.english: “Just for reference... What's this key for? What kind of catch comes with it?”

lines.japanese: 『へ？　聞きたい？』
lines.english: “Huh? You wanna know?”

lines.japanese: 「聞かない方がいいと思うぜえ？　おまえ芝居ヘタそうだし、知っちゃったらポリに上手く嘘つけねえだろ」
lines.english: “I don't think you should. You're a lousy actor. Once you know, you'll never lie convincingly to the cops.”

lines.japanese: 「事情聴取されること前提なのかよ……」
lines.english: “You're already assuming I'll be questioned by the police...?”

lines.japanese: アタマいてえ。一瞬でも揺らいだ俺が馬鹿だった。
lines.english: My head hurt. I'd been an idiot to waver even for a second.

lines.japanese: 「話になんねえわ。やっぱ他あたれ。じゃあな」
lines.english: “Forget it. Ask somebody else. Later.”

lines.japanese: 『ちょちょちょ、待てって！　頼むよ、これには俺の人生がかかって──』
lines.english: “W-w-wait! Please, my whole life depends on—”

lines.japanese: 「知るか」
lines.english: “Like I care.”

lines.japanese: 俺は親指でエージを黙らせた。
lines.english: I silenced Eiji with my thumb.

lines.japanese: 意外や再コールはなかったが、もう寝なおす気分でもなかった。
lines.english: Surprisingly, he didn't call back. But I was no longer in the mood to return to sleep.

lines.japanese: のそのそベッドを這いだして、分厚い遮光カーテンを開ける。曇り空に霞む正午過ぎの太陽が、だだっ広い部屋にひとりの俺をやんわりと射した。
lines.english: I crawled out of bed and opened the heavy blackout curtains. The hazy afternoon sun filtered through the cloudy sky and gently illuminated me alone in the cavernous room.

lines.japanese: １月上旬。鳴は二週間の冬休みを終えて、憂鬱な愚痴をこぼしながらもまた学校へ通いはじめていた。
lines.english: It was early January. Naru's two-week winter break had ended, and despite her gloomy complaints, she had started going to school again.

lines.japanese: テーブルに書き置きが残っている。
lines.english: She'd left a note on the table.

lines.japanese: 『おはようございますわ。キッチンに豪華な朝食を用意してございますわ。たんとお食べあそばせますわ』
lines.english: “Good morning, good sir. A sumptuous breakfast awaits you in the kitchen. Pray eat your fill.”

lines.japanese: ホホホ、と紙面の隅でキテレツな自画像が笑っていた。
lines.english: In one corner of the page, a bizarre self-portrait laughed, “Ho ho ho.”

lines.japanese: ごっつぁんですわ、と書きくわえて俺は部屋を移った。
lines.english: I added, “Much obliged, milady,” and moved to the other room.

lines.japanese: カップ麺、割り箸、電気ポット。
lines.english: Cup noodles, disposable chopsticks, an electric kettle.

lines.japanese: おっしゃる通り、豪華なブレックファーストが用意されていた。
lines.english: Just as she'd promised, a sumptuous breakfast awaited me.

lines.japanese: やつは自分じゃ手料理が得意な口ぶりだけれど、たまにここへ訪れる兄の証言によれば「玉子焼きが作れる程度のことを得意って呼んでいいなら、まあ、そうなんじゃない？」とのこと。
lines.english: She talked like she was a good cook, but according to her brother, who dropped by now and then, “If being able to make a rolled omelet counts as being good at cooking, then sure, I guess she is.”

lines.japanese: だから、クソ忙しい平日の朝にわざわざ手間のかかることはしなくていい、と申しでたのは俺の方だ。
lines.english: I was the one who told her she didn't need to go to extra trouble on a busy weekday morning.

lines.japanese: 学校へ行くってだけでも相当面倒くさいことなのに、その上メシのために早起きさせるなんて拷問だ。
lines.english: Going to school was enough of a pain already. Making her wake up early to cook on top of that would be torture.

lines.japanese: 「学校か……」
lines.english: “School, huh...”

lines.japanese: 偉いよなあ。あんな息詰まるハコに毎日行くんだから。
lines.english: Pretty impressive, really. She went to that suffocating box every single day.

lines.japanese: 「俺には無理だ」
lines.english: “I couldn’t do it.”

lines.japanese: カップ麺に湯を入れながら考えた。
lines.english: I thought about it as I poured hot water into the cup.

lines.japanese: “羽田鷹志”は私立美空学園に在籍中だ。
lines.english: “Takashi Haneda” was still enrolled at the private Misora Academy.

lines.japanese: だから本当は俺も、いなくなったタカシに代わってそこへ通わなければならない。
lines.english: So strictly speaking, I should have been attending in the vanished Takashi's place.

lines.japanese: しかし聞けば、受験生には三学期から自由登校が認められているらしい（もちろん俺に進学する気などないが“羽田鷹志”は受験生という扱いだった）。
lines.english: But from what I’d heard, students taking entrance exams could choose whether to attend from the third term on. I had no plans to go on to college, of course, but “Takashi Haneda” was down as an exam candidate.

lines.japanese: それでなくとも、やつが三年間がんばってくれたおかげで、卒業だけならもう黙っていても出来るという話だった。
lines.english: Besides, he'd worked hard for three years, so apparently I could graduate now without doing another thing.

lines.japanese: だから俺は、羽田の両親の許可を得て、学校へは行かず一足早く（フリーターとしてだが）社会へ出ることを志願した。
lines.english: I had therefore obtained the Hanedas' permission to skip school and enter the working world a little early—as a part-timer, admittedly.

lines.japanese: いまは夕方から飲食店、深夜から工事現場と、ふたつ掛け持ちで働かせてもらっている。
lines.english: These days I worked two jobs: at a restaurant from the evening, then at a construction site late at night.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: そろそろラーメン食うか、と思ったところでケータイが震えた。
lines.english: Just as I was thinking the noodles ought to be ready, my phone vibrated.

lines.japanese: エージからのメールだった。
lines.english: It was a message from Eiji.

lines.japanese: 『例のモノ、おパルさんに預けとくからヨロシＱ！』
lines.english: “I'll leave the thing with Paru, so thank-Q!”

lines.japanese: 『あと俺のこのケータイ、今から証拠隠滅でバキッと行っちゃうんで！　しばらく連絡つかないかもしんないけどゴメンＰ！』
lines.english: “Also, I'm about to snap this phone in half to destroy the evidence! Sorry if you can't reach me for a while, sorr-E!”

lines.japanese: 「うぜえ……」
lines.english: “What a pain...”

lines.japanese: メシが不味くなる。預かんねえって言ってんだろブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。
lines.english: He'd ruined my appetite. I told you I'm not holding it, you bastard. I'll fucking kill you.

lines.japanese: とそのまま打って返信してやった。
lines.english: I typed exactly that and sent it back.
